name: Pilar 7 Bridge Experience
seoTitle: Pilar 7 Bridge Viewpoint: 372 Steps While Lift Is Out
tagline: A visitor centre inside a pillar of the 25 de Abril Bridge, with a viewing platform 80 metres up that is currently reached only by stairs.

description.short: Pilar 7 Bridge Experience is a small visitor centre inside one of the 25 de Abril Bridge's pillars in Alcântara, with a viewing platform 80 metres up. The lift is under maintenance, so the platform is reached by 372 steps. Open daily 10:00–18:00.
description.full:
Know this before you go: the lift inside Pilar 7 is under maintenance, and the only way up to the viewing platform is 372 steps, about 80 metres up the pillar. Visit Lisboa, which sells the tickets, flags the lift problem on its pages and has cut the online price to €3 for every ticket type while it lasts. If you have mobility problems, heart trouble or little time, skip it: the ground-floor model room and virtual reality booth are not worth the trip on their own.

If you are fit and want the view, it is one you cannot get elsewhere. From the platform, part of which has a glass floor, you look across the Tagus to Cristo Rei on the south bank, down on the Alcântara docks and east towards the city centre, with the bridge's steelwork close by.

Getting there: it is about 5.2 km from the terminal. Take a Cascais-line train from Cais do Sodré to Alcântara-Mar and walk a short way to Avenida da Índia, or take a taxi, which takes 12–15 minutes. Tram 15E also stops at Alcântara.

Opening hours are 10:00 to 18:00 daily, with last entry at 17:00; it is closed on 25 December. Allow about an hour inside, more if you rest on the stairs. The platform is exposed, so bring a layer and skip the visit on a day of low cloud or strong wind. Visitors have also reported closed rooms and out-of-order toilets during the lift outage, so set your expectations accordingly.

It works best paired with LX Factory, about 15 minutes' walk inland, or as a stop on the way west to Belém.

Context: the attraction opened in 2017, giving the public access to the inside of the bridge for the first time.
description.history: The suspension bridge across the Tagus was built between 1962 and 1966 and opened on 6 August 1966 as the Ponte Salazar, named after the dictator. After the Carnation Revolution of 25 April 1974 it was renamed after that date. Its main span is 1,013 metres, and a lower railway deck opened in 1999, carrying trains to the south bank. The Pilar 7 project, inaugurated on 27 September 2017, opened one of the pillars on the Alcântara side to visitors, with an exhibition on the bridge's construction, a model room, virtual reality and a viewing platform 80 metres above the ground.
description.significance: The 25 de Abril Bridge was the first fixed crossing of the Tagus at Lisbon, and it changed how the city and the south bank grew. Its name records the end of the dictatorship. Pilar 7 is the only place where the public can go up inside the structure, which is the one thing here that a riverside photo cannot give you.

directions.general: Located in Alcântara district along Avenida da Índia waterfront, directly beneath the Ponte 25 de Abril suspension bridge
directions.fromCruisePort: About 5.2 km west, at the foot of the 25 de Abril Bridge in Alcântara. Taxi about 12-15 minutes, or the train from Cais do Sodré to Alcântara-Mar and a short walk.

tips: The lift is out of service and the viewing platform is 372 steps up; check the Visit Lisboa page for the lift status before you set off.
Online tickets from the Visit Lisboa shop are €3 for all ages while the lift is under maintenance (normally €5.50 adult); children up to 5 go free, and entry is free with the Lisboa Card.
Virtual reality is an optional €1.50 add-on; skip it if you are short of time.
Open daily 10:00–18:00 with last entry at 17:00; closed on 25 December.
Take a Cascais-line train from Cais do Sodré to Alcântara-Mar and walk a short way to Avenida da Índia, or take a taxi from the terminal (12–15 minutes).
The platform is exposed: bring a layer and skip the visit on low-cloud or very windy days.
Pair it with LX Factory, about 15 minutes' walk inland, for a half day west of the centre.
Use the toilets before you arrive; visitors have reported facilities out of order during the lift outage.

highlights: Viewing platform 80 metres up, partly glass-floored, currently reached by 372 steps
Views across the Tagus to Cristo Rei and over the Alcântara docks
Close-up view of the bridge's steelwork
Model room and exhibition on the bridge's construction
Mirror room and cable room on the 4th floor
Optional virtual reality experience of inaccessible parts of the bridge (€1.50)
facilities: Gift shop (10% off with the Lisboa Card)
Toilets (reported out of order at times)

accessibility.mobilityNotes: While the lift is under maintenance the viewing platform and upper rooms are reached only by stairs (372 steps to the platform). Only the ground floor is accessible without climbing.
